name: Guru
description: Guru is an enterprise knowledge-management platform that organizes and continuously verifies company information — policies, procedures, product info — so employees and connected AI tools can retrieve accurate, permission-scoped answers.
best_for: Positioned for enterprise organizations — HR, Ops, Support, Sales, Engineering, L&D — across industries like tech, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing.
cons: No public self-serve pricing exists at all -- every plan routes to "Talk to sales," and the official pricing page states investment is tailored to organization scale rather than listing any tier or seat price.

This is a reversal from Guru's own prior marketing: the company once advertised a forever-free Starter plan for up to 10 users, but that plan no longer appears anywhere on the current pricing page or homepage.

Guru's own pricing copy frames cost around an organization's "AI maturity" as an explicit, unquantified pricing lever, meaning AI-related knowledge features are a real cost variable buyers cannot estimate without a sales engagement.
features: Knowledge structuring and governance with continuous review
Knowledge Agents that verify content and draft documentation
Automated quality control: conflict detection, duplicate merging, stale-content flagging
Integrations with Slack, Microsoft Teams, and AI tools
